
`lode doc edit` and `lode doc revise --file` on a spec are editing conveniences that write rules. `lode doc show <ref> --editable` renders each anchored heading with its rule ref as a Pandoc attribute, `## 3. Leases {#sec-3 rule=<rule ref>}`, and the write accepts that form back. A heading naming a rule is the placeholder: it arranges that rule at that position, whichever spec it came from, and changed text under it is a rule edit (WL-REQ-1298). A heading with no rule ref goes through the three-pass match of WL-SPEC-77#sec-4g against the spec's own rules, and an unmatched heading becomes a new rule. Text outside every rule's body is template text and is written to the spec. A rule the write leaves out is unarranged, not withdrawn. A heading naming a withdrawn rule is refused with the rule's successors named, unless the spec already arranges it and the text under it is unchanged. The `rule=` attribute appears only in the editable form.
